title: 5d-5: constraint waivers (DB)
description:
## Parent

sutra/68 — 5d PRD: constraint system + DD integration

## What to build

Durable `constraint_waivers` table following the same pattern as `convention_waivers`. Stores accepted constraint violations with rationale. Waivers target a specific constraint + file/symbol scope. Survives reindex. Includes CRUD methods on `Db` and orphan detection for waivers whose constraint no longer exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Durable `constraint_waivers` table with migration
- [ ] CRUD methods on `Db`
- [ ] Waivers survive reindex
- [ ] Orphan detection
- [ ] Tests for CRUD, durability, orphans

## Blocked by

- sutra/70 — 5d-2: constraint types + rules parsing

acceptance_criteria.text: New constraint_waivers durable table: constraint_id TEXT, file_path TEXT, symbol_qualified_name TEXT (nullable), rationale TEXT NOT NULL, created_at, updated_at
Migration registered with ephemeral_only: false, table in TABLE_REGISTRY as Durable
CRUD methods on Db: create_constraint_waiver, get_constraint_waivers, get_constraint_waivers_for_file, update_constraint_waiver, delete_constraint_waiver
Waivers reference constraints by hash or name
Orphan detection: waivers for constraints no longer in rules.toml surfaced in reconciliation
Tests cover: CRUD, reindex survival, scoping by file/symbol, orphan detection

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention. 1 medium finding on waiver upsert.

1. [medium] create_constraint_waiver returns last_insert_rowid() after ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, which is not set to the updated row's id — it remains the last successful INSERT id on the connection. Callers trusting the return value could update/delete the wrong waiver. Fix: use RETURNING id, or SELECT id by unique key after upsert.

Next: add upsert-conflict test asserting the returned id matches the existing row."
